run.question:
Alertmanager alert PendingPodsDetected (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/otel-demo since 2026-11-16T17:45:49Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The PendingPodsDetected alert is explained by two unschedulable pods in namespace otel-demo: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh (cluster-wide Pending count is exactly 2, matching the alert's 'current: 2'). Both pods carry nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node, a hostname that no node in the cluster has; the scheduler reports PodScheduled=False/Unschedulable with '0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector'. The selector comes from the pod templates of Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart (revision 2, both the only deployments cluster-wide with this value; the value is not present in any readable ConfigMap). Ownership chain: the two Pending pods are owned by ReplicaSets ad-dd7f45975 (created 17:44:52Z) and cart-5b597c6db5 (created 17:45:00Z), which are owned by Deployments ad and cart; the previous ReplicaSets of the same deployments (created 17:07Z, no nodeSelector) still run one Ready replica each, and both Services still have one ready endpoint, so the workloads remained Available (1 ready, 1 unavailable each) rather than fully down. Node capacity, node readiness, taints and resource pressure were checked and do not explain the failures. Impact evidence is confined to the two Pending pods and their two owning Deployments; no other workload in the cluster has a Pending pod or the invalid selector.

claims.text: At 18:00:37Z, 2 of 23 pods in otel-demo were Pending: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p and cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh; the other 21 pods (including ad-554b849958-42mdm and cart-755465879b-bgb2p) were Running. A cluster-wide count of Pending pods returned exactly these same 2 pods, matching the alert annotation's 'current: 2'.

Both Pending pods have status condition PodScheduled=False with reason Unschedulable and message '0/5 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had untolerated taint {node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: }, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/5 nodes are available: 5 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.', and both specify nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"}. Pod ad-dd7f45975-mw86p is owned by ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975; pod cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh by ReplicaSet cart-5b597c6db5.

The cluster has 5 nodes, all with Ready=True: i-01a47734339426210 (control-plane, taint node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule), and i-037e40963128cbd9f, i-0424ef08cd107882f, i-08831c4b8af18ed15, i-097278082719f10ba (no taints, label node-role.kubernetes.io/node). No node carries kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node; the hostname labels are the node names above.

Deployments ad and cart in otel-demo both carry nodeSelector {"kubernetes.io/hostname":"invalid-node"} in .spec.template.spec.nodeSelector, with deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=2 and generation=2 (equal to status.observedGeneration). Each has spec.replicas=1 but status.replicas=2, readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1, unavailableReplicas=1, and a Progressing condition citing the new ReplicaSet (ad-dd7f45975, cart-5b597c6db5).

Across all 36 deployments in the cluster, only otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart have a pod-template nodeSelector of kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node; the other deployments with any nodeSelector (ingress-nginx-controller, cilium-operator, coredns, coredns-autoscaler, ebs-csi-controller, opentelemetry-operator) use kubernetes.io/os=linux. A search of statefulsets for the same value returned nothing.

Ownership chain and rollout history: ReplicaSet ad-dd7f45975 (created 2026-11-16T17:44:52Z, nodeSelector invalid-node, readyReplicas null) and cart-5b597c6db5 (created 2026-11-16T17:45:00Z, same nodeSelector, readyReplicas null) are owned by Deployments ad (uid 9f4f1390-79dc-46c5-8574-20a4de0f4054) and cart (uid 4b8a64b0-64d6-4c21-95b7-253fbc26d708) respectively. The earlier ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and cart-755465879b (created 17:07:26-27Z, nodeSelector null) still each have desired=1, ready=1, available=1.

Namespace events in the window tie the Pending pods to a scale-up of the new ReplicaSets: 'Scaled up replica set ad-dd7f45975 from 0 to 1' and 'Created pod: ad-dd7f45975-mw86p' at 17:44:52Z; 'Scaled up replica set cart-5b597c6db5 from 0 to 1' and 'Created pod: cart-5b597c6db5-pkzkh' at 17:45:00Z; plus Warning FailedScheduling on each of the two pods with the same '0/5 nodes are available' message, count 3, last seen 17:55:15Z.

Despite the two Pending pods, Services ad (selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad) and cart (selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart) each still have one ready endpoint address (100.96.3.180 and 100.96.3.205, port 8080) and no not-ready addresses, consistent with the surviving older ReplicaSet replicas.
No ConfigMap in the cluster contains the string 'invalid-node' in its data (55 ConfigMaps processed), so the value in the two pod templates is not explained by any readable ConfigMap.

The Prometheus target exposes 63 metric names in the window, dominated by container/cAdvisor, JVM/process, traces_span_metrics* and redis metrics; no kube_pod_status_phase, kube_deployment_status_* or other kube-state-metrics pod/deployment status series are in that inventory, and a direct query on kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="otel-demo",phase="Pending"} returned no series. The Pending state is therefore evidenced from the Kubernetes API, not from this Prometheus.

Span-status counts over the 16:45:49-18:00:35 window (span counts, not request counts) are: ad STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 3.046875 and STATUS_CODE_UNSET 4387.68115942029; cart STATUS_CODE_ERROR absent (no series returned) and STATUS_CODE_UNSET 38901.739130434784. The sampled ad error spans are flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans with rpc.grpc.status_code="4" that started at 17:13:21Z and 17:23:18Z, i.e. before the 17:44:52Z ReplicaSet scale-up, so they are not caused by the Pending pods.

The control-plane taint does not explain the failures: only 1 of the 5 nodes (i-01a47734339426210) carries node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule, while the other 4 nodes are Ready, untainted and rejected the pods solely because of the pod's node affinity/selector.

Node resource exhaustion (insufficient CPU/memory) is not the cause: the FailedScheduling message lists only an untolerated control-plane taint and a node affinity/selector mismatch, with 'preemption: ... 5 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling' and no Insufficient cpu/memory reason, and all 4 worker nodes are Ready.

A missing or unhealthy node pool is not the cause: all 5 nodes report Ready=True, so no node was down or NotReady at the time of the query; the rejections are selector-driven rather than an absence of schedulable capacity.

The invalid nodeSelector was introduced by a configuration change to the pod templates of Deployments ad and cart at about 17:44:52-17:45:00Z (deployment revision 2, generation 2, new ReplicaSets created 17:44:52Z/17:45:00Z while the 17:07Z ReplicaSets have no nodeSelector), plausibly a Helm upgrade of release otel-demo (each Deployment carries meta.helm.sh/release-name=otel-demo), but the actor and the exact change mechanism cannot be confirmed without change history or the Helm release values.

The two Deployments are not out of service: each still has readyReplicas=1 and Available=True (MinimumReplicasAvailable), and the ad/cart Service endpoints each contain one ready address, so the evidence shows a stuck rollout with reduced replica capacity (1 of 2 desired pods serving per workload), not a full outage of ad or cart.

Remove or correct the nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node in the pod templates of Deployments otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart (or set a real hostname), then let the rollout replace ReplicaSets ad-dd7f45975 and cart-5b597c6db5 and confirm the two Pending pods disappear.

Review and correct the Helm values/chart input for release otel-demo (namespace otel-demo) that produced deployment revision 2, so the same hostname value is not re-applied on the next upgrade; the release values are stored in a Secret that this investigation cannot read.

gaps: The alerting rule PendingPodsDetected was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (view 9939d0c5-7251-41f2-a56d-6d95cb823312-t0:8677406f-3f6a-4542-96f6-d7a5847fc510, status no_data), and this Prometheus exposes no kube-state-metrics pod/deployment status series (kube_pod_status_phase query 9939d0c5-7251-41f2-a56d-6d95cb823312-t1:f3d61100-f2c9-41c8-968c-7bf614e094fb returned no_data; metric inventory 968b2ad5-2d05-4b0d-bdb5-cf2707304f9c-t0 has 63 names with no kube_* status metrics), so the alert's exact expression and the value that fired it could not be verified in this target.

The change_history integration is not available, so who or what set nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node at ~17:44:52-17:45:00Z, and whether it came from a Helm upgrade of release otel-demo or a direct patch, is unverified; Helm release values live in a Secret that cannot be read.

The two traces_search views for ad (1fee3966-9668-4dbe-a4be-e17baa444d6d-t1) and cart (1fee3966-9668-4dbe-a4be-e17baa444d6d-t2) both returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE (status error, 393 and 715 spans), so those span populations were not read in full and the sampled span view is not a complete call chain.

Application logs of the two Pending pods do not exist because their containers were never started (no node assigned); the log reads for the surviving pods ad-554b849958-42mdm (add20ddd-dfb5-4ea1-8830-1909d59f776b-t0:38c4efe6-b5a8-4d12-92e9-4f1eedc476cf) and cart-755465879b-bgb2p (add20ddd-dfb5-4ea1-8830-1909d59f776b-t1:86739f67-21f5-4dcf-ab36-eed5cd548455) both returned no_data for the error-pattern filter in 17:30-18:00Z, so application health of the surviving replicas is not established by logs.

Trace data available in Jaeger ends at source_end_at 2026-11-16T17:33:18Z (freshness ~1663s at 18:01Z), so any span behaviour after 17:33Z is unknown, including the period right after the 17:44-17:45Z rollout; cart error-tag search (968b2ad5-2d05-4b0d-bdb5-cf2707304f9c-t2:8c1237e0-24b3-4c7b-8b93-db38e9ef2eb1) returned no_data, which is unknown rather than zero errors.
No evidence was gathered on controllers outside the cluster that might re-apply the pod template (for example CI/CD or GitOps); that data source is not part of this Run.
next_steps: Correct the nodeSelector kubernetes.io/hostname=invalid-node in the pod templates of otel-demo/ad and otel-demo/cart (or set a real node hostname) and let the rollout replace ReplicaSets ad-dd7f45975 and cart-5b597c6db5, confirming the Pending pods clear.

Review the Helm values or chart input for release otel-demo that produced deployment revision 2 so the invalid hostname is not re-applied, and record who applied the change using the change-history source when it is available.
Inspect the PendingPodsDetected rule definition in the alerting Prometheus, and add/verify kube-state-metrics kube_pod_status_phase series so pod-phase alerts can be validated from metrics.

After the fix, re-check that ad and cart return to 2 ready replicas each and verify span error rates for ad, since ad showed 2 sampled flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans with rpc.grpc.status_code="4" before the rollout.
